title: Drops Before the Retina Photo

patient.name: Mr Ramli bin Osman
patient.presenting_complaint: Here for diabetic retinal photography; needs dilating drops before the photos
patient.address: Blk 361 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, #08-178, Singapore 610027

history.hpc: Mr Ramli attends for diabetic eye screening with retinal photography, which needs his pupils dilated. He says: 'Nurse say must put drops to make my eye big big before take photo, then cannot drive after right?' He has no history of narrow angles or acute glaucoma. The PSA must prepare and instil dilating drops correctly and document the procedure.
history.pmhx: Type 2 diabetes. No previous acute glaucoma or narrow-angle problems.
history.social_hx: Bus captain; drove himself today (relevant to post-dilation advice).

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Normal; no shallow anterior chamber concerns reported

investigations.pupil_dilation: Dilation prepared: confirm the eye(s) to dilate (both), record pre-dilation pupil size in mm (RE and LE), check for contraindications (narrow angles/previous acute glaucoma — none here), confirm no drop allergy. Instil dilating drops (e.g., tropicamide 1% +/- phenylephrine 2.5%) with correct technique, record dosage (number of instillations) and time. Allow time to take effect before photography.
investigations.documentation: Eye(s) to dilate, pre-dilation pupil sizes, drops used, number of instillations, time given.

diagnosis: Routine pupil dilation to enable diabetic retinal photography. The PSA competency is the correct, safe dilation workflow — checking contraindications/allergy, correct instillation technique, accurate documentation, and clear post-dilation safety advice (especially about driving).

immediate: Confirm the indication and which eye(s) to dilate, and check for contraindications (narrow angles/previous acute glaucoma) and drop allergy
Record the pre-dilation pupil size in mm for each eye
Instil the dilating drops with correct technique (head back, pull down lower lid, drop into the lower fornix, ask the patient to close gently)
Record the drug, dosage (number of instillations), eye(s), and the time given
Warn the patient about blurred near vision and light sensitivity for 4-6 hours
Advise he should not drive after dilation and arrange alternative transport
follow_up: Proceed to retinal photography once adequately dilated
Doctor/screening service to review the images
Document the dilation details in the record
patient_education: Explain the drops make the pupil big so the retina can be photographed
Warn that near vision will be blurry and eyes light-sensitive for about 4-6 hours
Advise not to drive while dilated and to arrange another way home
Offer sunglasses/UV protectors for comfort after dilation

key_points: Confirms the indication (diabetic retinal photography) and eye(s) to dilate
Checks for contraindications (narrow angle/previous acute glaucoma)
Identifies that the patient drove himself (relevant to advice)
Records pre-dilation pupil size in mm for each eye
Uses correct instillation technique into the lower fornix
Records the drug, dosage (instillations), eye(s), and time
Allows adequate time for dilation before photography
Understands the purpose of dilation for fundus photography
Knows the common dilating drops and the need to check contraindications
Recognises the expected duration of blurred near vision/photosensitivity (4-6 hours)
Knows dilation increases short-term risk (driving, falls)
Warns about blurred vision and photosensitivity
Advises against driving and helps arrange transport
Offers sunglasses and clear post-dilation advice
